proof_numbered:
0001 | I have the following proof: let $G$ be a graph with $n$ vertices and $n-1$ edges, prove that $G$ is connected iff $G$ has no cycles.
0002 | 
0003 | I proceed proving "only if" first.  Assume $G$ has some cycle consuming $|C| \le n$ vertices and $|C|$ edges.  We are thus left to try and connect $n-|C|$ vertices and $n-1-|C|$ edges.  This subgraph must contain at least $|C|+1$ connected components and because $|C| \gt 0$, $|C|+1 \gt 1$, therefore G cannot be connected.
0004 | 
0005 | Now proving that if $G$ has no cycles, then it is connected.  Because $G$ has $n \epsilon N, n \gt 0$ vertices, we can walk along them, connecting them.  Take $v \epsilon V, v={v_1, ..., v_n}$ where $|v|=n$.  Then first connect $v_1$ and $v_2$, consuming one edge.  Then connect $v_2$ and $v_3$ consuming another edge.  Proceed this way until $v_{n-1}$ and $v_n$ are connected, after which point, $n-1$ edges will have been consumed.  $v$ clearly has no cycles and is connected.  
0006 | 
0007 | Does this proof look correct?
